newsitem.title: UK: Ghana '96/97 cocoa crop put at 320,000/340,000 tns.
newsitem.headline: Ghana '96/97 cocoa crop put at 320,000/340,000 tns.

text.p: Ghana's total cocoa crop, which includes the light crop, will be between 320,000 and 340,000 tonnes in the current 1996/97 season, John Henry Newman, Chief Executuive of Ghana Cocoa Board said on Thursday.
"It will be much much lower (the crop) this year. Last year it was extraordinary. I think you can call it almost a fluke last year."
"This year, rains were slightly too early. It caused a small dent in production," Newman told reporters on the sidelines of the International Cocoa Organization (ICCO) meeting in London.
Growing conditions were not as ideal as last year, and black pod was a problem, he said.
He said the estimate for the 1995/96 crop was finalised at 400,000 tonnes, which included the light crop.

He added that although 1996/97 purchases were about 20 percent below comparative weeks of last year, they would show a slight improvement from February 1997 because of good rains in key production areas.
"I think overall the reduction in purchases will be around 15 percent. If we get a couple of more rains we will get a good light crop," he said.

Newman added that the main crop would be between 290,000 and 300,000 tonnes. The forecast for this year's total crop was 320,000/330,000 tonnes, but it would reach 340,000 tonnes if there was a long tail.
